promises.promise: Loom is a program one household runs for itself. A few people and a few AI agents share a desk in the browser: small app windows side by side, the agents at the edge, a ticker along the top.

Whatever an agent does, it does in a conversation. You chat with it in loom. Someone talks to it on Discord or Slack. A trigger starts it. One agent hands work to another. Each of these is the same thing to loom, so conversations sit at the centre and every other part touches them.
Chat is how you control loom. Screens are for seeing. Every app also appears inline in a conversation.

1 Chat controls, screens show You control loom by talking to your agents. Screens are for seeing. A settings change or a dangerous action asked for in chat gets an approval card inline, with before and after. Ordinary work needs no card.
2 Installed means trusted Loom's own parts never ask each other for permission. Loom checks permission only for callers from outside.
3 A small team that trusts each other The project is the unit of sharing. No fine-grained permissions. Household owners see everything.
4 Real columns Every fact is a named column, defined once with Drizzle. The database does the work. SQLite by default; the database is a configuration choice.
5 One query endpoint A GraphQL endpoint generated from the same schema. A tile names the fields it wants, and changes arrive as subscriptions over one websocket.
6 Only memories are precious Agents' memories are the one kind of data loom treats as irreplaceable. Notes come second: looked after, but not irreplaceable.
7 One program, one data folder Quick for someone else to install. One API for the command line, the web app and agents. A restart is an acceptable deploy.
8 Parts can be replaced Each part is a module with a typed interface, so the task store or a bridge can be swapped for another.
